mutants.why: the header name is the text BEFORE the colon; left(colon + 1) folds the ':' into the name so a Content-Type lookup keyed on the bare token misses
the value starts one byte AFTER the colon; mid(colon) prefixes every value with a stray ':' that trimming cannot strip
a folded continuation line must be joined to the preceding value with a single space; dropping it concatenates the two tokens ("folded valuecontinued")

the continuation line's own leading whitespace (space/tab indent) must be stripped before joining; keeping it leaves embedded double spaces / tabs inside the value that the final outer trim cannot reach

'From : x' (space before the colon) yields the raw name 'From ', so the name must be trimmed before use; without it the key is 'from ' and every bare-token lookup misses. This is the ONLY trim applied to the name (extraction does not trim), so removing it is observable

the CRLF header/body boundary is the blank line 

; matching a single 
 cuts the block after the first header, dropping every header after the first from a CRLF message

the LF-only boundary is the blank line 

; matching a single 
 cuts the block after the first header, dropping every header after the first from an LF-only message

colon == 0 means a leading-colon line with no name; with > 0 it is skipped, with >= 0 the name is left(0) == "" and flushHeader's !current_name.isEmpty() guard drops it anyway. indexOf returns -1 when absent (fails both tests). The emitted map is byte-identical for every input

this entry previously claimed 'equivalent' on the grounds that flushHeader trims the value a SECOND time before insertion. That reasoning is WRONG, and was masked by a corpus in which no value carried trailing whitespace that was then FOLDED. The two trims are not interchangeable: whatever this one leaves on the value is carried INTO the fold join (current_value += ' ' + continuation), which puts it in the MIDDLE of the string where the outer trim can no longer reach it. 'Content-Type: text/plain;   ' folded onto ' charset=utf-8' yields 'text/plain;    charset=utf-8' (four spaces) instead of one, and a downstream charset/boundary split mis-tokenises it. Killed by foldedContinuationJoinsWithSingleSpace
